plan.title: Reduce overhead for vBRIEF phase lifecycle completion

narratives.Description: Lifecycle completion after a product PR merges costs extra PRs, operator hand-offs and fragile batch runs. This story lands the accepted Prefer-A Recut-3 Bound: completion admission reuses the #5710 merge-time bases, issue-less briefs join the same owed discovery, one refused story no longer fails a batched finalize, lifecycle-only PRs need no new CHANGELOG line, and lifecycle verbs write their own CHANGELOG and spec-drift-ledger output.
narratives.Overview:
- relieves: P1 — Drop Prefer-A's keyword-only close refusal. Admission for issue-tied completion reuses `evaluateDeliveryGate` / `verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity` merge-time bases already shipped by #5710 (a sole `deft-story` mark, b closing keyword, c Connected link as of `merged_at`). Work with no merge-time basis still refuses (`proveIssueAnchoredAssociation`). Prefer-A MUST NOT add a second admission refuse that contradicts those writers.
- relieves: P2 — Issue-less briefs are in scope for the same trigger and batched land when PR-only identity proves (`identityBasis: pr-only` / stamped `productPullRequest` + canonical remote). Remint `discoverFinalizeOwed` to admit tip nonterminal briefs with stamped `productPullRequest`, no github-issue origin, and pr-only-proofable identity (same discoverer; no parallel PR-only finalizer). Admitted record shape carries product PR without a forge issue (optional/null issue or explicit issue-less discriminant — not a fake `#0`). Skip origin-issue verify and origin-close for those rows; issue-tied path unchanged.
- relieves: P3 — One refused story MUST NOT fail the whole batched finalize. In `finalize-cohort.ts`, a refused `deft-story` mark records on a non-fatal pending/warnings channel (inventory: existing `pending` / `EXIT_INCOMPLETE` pattern) and leaves that story pending; stamp/sweep/commit/land continue for other admitted stories. Refused-mark outcomes MUST NOT alone satisfy fatal `errors.length > 0` for either whole-batch `skipSweep` conjunct, for commit/land gating, or for cohort `ok:false` / `EXIT_GATE_FAILED`. Preserve the #6212 invariant that refused marks never receive single-PR `defaultEvidence` / stamp. Real config/delivery errors stay fail-closed. Control-flow carve in the same writer; no second discoverer.
- relieves: P4 — `verify:changelog-unreleased` (against merge-base) exempts a change set that is delivery-brief-land-shaped after the co-extension below. Oracle: feed `git diff --name-only <merge-base>...HEAD` (or the existing delivery-evidence PR changed-files seam) into the extended `isDeliveryBriefLandExcluded`; on true, skip the against-merge-base **new-entry** compare only; product/code-bearing diffs keep today's requirement; empty change-set stays non-exempt (`files.length > 0` fail-closed). Gate change lands through this arc and review (#3156).
- relieves: P5 — `scope:activate`, `scope:complete`, and `swarm:finalize-cohort` write any still-required CHANGELOG Unreleased line and the completion-time spec-drift-ledger update as verb output (same hook authority as brief moves). Agents MUST NOT free-form those paths on lifecycle PRs. Membership admits exact `xbrief/.audit/spec-drift-ledger.json` only under delivery-brief-land / completion-move shape (#6231 class; not #6235).

### Mechanism limbs (Thin Fail-Closed)

- Co-extension (F1): when ledger is added to the delivery-brief-land family, `isDeliveryBriefLandPath` / `isDeliveryBriefLandExcluded` and `isLifecycleShapedPr` MUST stay co-extensive (shared helper, or an explicit twin update in `finalize-cohort.ts` in the same remint). Silent divergence is a reject.
- Held from Recut-2: post-merge trigger is a second caller of owed-discovery; publication idempotent; fixed FINALIZE_OWED_LABEL-shaped coalesce lane; shared ownership across trigger / finalize-owed / session-start; direct land only under positively typed opt-in AND direct-write policy AND forge permission; pre-land completed-write-guard with baseRef = pre-push remote tip.
- operator-deferred: measured ceremony dial / activation collapse remain on #6204 (and any residual of #6203 not already shipped)

Reuse evaluateDeliveryGate / verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity for completion admission and add no second refuse. Remint discoverFinalizeOwed (packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-owed.ts) to admit issue-less briefs with a stamped productPullRequest and pr-only identity, with an issue-less record shape and no origin-close. In finalize-cohort.ts, route a refused deft-story mark to the non-fatal pending channel so other stories still stamp, sweep and land, and keep the #6212 no-stamp invariant. Exempt delivery-brief-land change sets from the verify:changelog-unreleased new-entry compare (packages/core/src/platform/changelog-cli.ts and resolve-changelog-unreleased.ts), with an empty change set non-exempt. Have scope:activate, scope:complete and swarm:finalize-cohort write any required CHANGELOG line and the spec-drift-ledger update as verb output, and admit the exact ledger path in membership only under the completion-move shape (scope-provenance/base-fence.ts). Keep isDeliveryBriefLandPath / isDeliveryBriefLandExcluded and isLifecycleShapedPr co-extensive through one shared helper. Cover each limb with focused vitest cases and add a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

issueCommentThread.body: Internal benchmark evidence (2026-08-09; private section-31 note) now quantifies this overhead cluster: directive was the most expensive framework in every measured cell - roughly 3-6x turns and 2.7-6.9x dollars-per-point versus no framework - with zero aggregate score gain on the suite. Lifecycle writes are part of that fixed cost. The composing proposal is the ceremony dial in #3214; this issue is one of the levers it would scale down for small tasks.

New field data (consumer run, 0.129.6): 22 PRs, 6 carried product changes. Lifecycle PRs added about 8,100 lines of JSON against about 8,400 product lines. Every story paid a separate completion PR because `scope:complete` requires the product PR to be merged first (#3041 / #3675).

Options 4 and 5 in the body still look like the two clean exits:

- Post-merge automation: on merge, stamp `merged_pr` / `merged_commit` and land the completed brief (bot commit where branch policy allows, else one batched bot PR).
- Record completion outside the tracked tree, keyed to the merge commit, and derive `completed/` placement from it.

Interim, no new mechanism: make `swarm:finalize-cohort` the documented default for solo stories too, so completions batch into one lifecycle PR. Note the tension with #5736: it requires cohort leftover-complete to land before the next activation opens, so batching delays the next activation. The interim needs that refuse to admit an open batched finalize PR.

Related: #5710 / #3631 (PR-only and chore completion paths), #4012 (lifecycle-only CI lane for consumers), #6203 (brief + code in one PR), #6204 (small-change lane).

Correction to my earlier comment on the interim. Batching solo completions through `swarm:finalize-cohort` does not conflict with the #5736 leftover-before-activation refuse: the batch can land just before the next activation opens. But it saves nothing while each solo story has its own activation PR, because the batch must land before every activation and so holds one completion. The interim only pays when activations are batched too, or once #6203 removes the separate activation PR. The #5736 refuse does not need to change.

## In plain English

Every story still pays a second PR after the product merge just to move the brief to completed/ and stamp merge metadata. On a recent consumer run that was about half the PRs and half the lines, with almost no product value. Prefer-A keeps delivery provenance, but lands the completed brief through post-merge automation (bot commit when branch policy allows, else one batched bot PR) instead of a human/agent lifecycle PR per story. v1 does not heal already-merged stuck issue-tied briefs or keyword-only closes — those still fail (#5710 class).

## Approaches

### Approach A (Prefer-A lean) — body option 4
- Keep scope:complete filesystem-only and merge-gated (#3041 / #3675).
- After product merge, automation stamps merged_pr / merged_commit and lands the completed brief.
- Land path: direct bot commit on the delivery branch when plan.policy / branch protection admits it; otherwise open one bot-owned batched lifecycle PR that may carry N completions.
- Reuse leftover-complete / swarm:finalize-cohort writers for the bytes; automation owns the land trigger that today is a manual second PR.
- Interim (doc-only until automation ships): default solo stories through finalize-cohort batching; note it only saves PRs when activations batch or #6203 collapses activation.

### Approach B — body option 5
- Move completion SoT off the tracked tree (ledger keyed to merge commit); derive completed/ placement from that ledger. Bigger SoT cut; higher blast.

### Approach C — body option 1
- Fold completion into the product PR before merge. Reject as primary: merge SHA / merged_pr are unknown pre-merge.

### Approach D — body option 2 alone
- Ad-hoc human direct commits for lifecycle only. Weak audit; conflicts with requireHumanMerge / branch protection norms.

## Proposed Bound remedy (draft — bind after Round-1)

- relieves: P1 — Post-merge automation stamps merged_pr / merged_commit after product merge without a human-authored lifecycle PR
- relieves: P2 — Land completed brief via bot commit when policy allows, else one batched bot lifecycle PR (N completions per land)
- relieves: P3 — Reuse leftover-complete / finalize-cohort byte writers; automation is the land trigger, not a parallel stamp format
- relieves: P4 — Document solo to finalize-cohort interim and the #6203 / batched-activation dependency; do not pretend interim alone clears P2 while activations stay 1:1
- Footnote: CHANGELOG / scm docs for bot-land vs batched-PR; ceremony-dial pointer to #6204 / #3214
- Footnote / non-claim: v1 automation admits only clean post-merge leftover-complete candidates; already-merged stuck issue-tied + keyword-only closes remain out of scope (still fail)

## Reject

- Approach C pre-merge completion as primary (unknown merge metadata)
- Approach D ad-hoc human direct-commit as the durable close
- Dropping merged_pr / merged_commit provenance without a replacement SoT
- Claiming v1 automation completes already-merged stuck issue-tied briefs or keyword-only closes (#5710 class)
- Softening #3041 / #3675 merge-before-complete
- Claiming finalize-cohort solo batching alone removes per-story lifecycle PRs while activation stays 1:1 (#6203)
- Absorbing #6203 same-PR brief+code or #6204 small-change lane into this Bound

## file_scope (lean)

- packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts (+ post-merge land trigger / bot-PR path as needed)
- packages/core/src/scope/** or leftover-complete land helpers that stamp delivery provenance
- packages/cli or tasks surface for the automation entry (webhook/Action/verb) if required
- content docs / scm/github.md pointer for bot-land vs batched lifecycle PR
- CHANGELOG.md

## Keep-outs

- #6203 forge-attested same-PR brief+code (activation collapse)
- #6204 / #3214 ceremony dial / small-change lane
- #5710 already-merged stuck issue-tied briefs and keyword-only closes: v1 post-merge automation MUST NOT claim to complete those; they stay fail / residual (operator cue on arc 680)
- #5710 PR-only complete path (adjacent; see stuck/keyword keep-out above)
- #3631 chore provenance model
- #4012 lifecycle-only CI lane shape (may compose later; not this Bound)
- Rewriting requireHumanMerge / branch-protection policy as this ticket

All three fixes are one clause. None re-architects the Bound.

## Audit by pain

### P1 — honest, with one wording overstatement

`sharpening`

The P1 limb is mechanically clean: `evaluateDeliveryGate` then `stampDeliveryProvenance`, no parallel stamp writer, field names corrected to `completionProvenance.{prNumber, mergeCommit, deliveryCommit, disposition}` (F4 landed). The #5710 fail-closed limb matches the operator limit exactly.

But `relieves: P1` overstates what happens. P1's pain is that merge-gating *forces a post-merge write on every shipped story*. The Bound's own Reject line refuses to soften #3041 / #3675 — so the per-story write survives intact. What changes is **who authors it**, not whether it exists. Honest form: `absorbs: P1 — per-story post-merge write held invariant; relief is authorship only`. This matters because P1-as-relieved plus P2-as-limited reads, to a later reader, as though the structural cost were addressed somewhere. It is not addressed anywhere in this Bound, by design.

### P2 — direct-land admission is satisfied by silence

`blocking` · harvest-changed

The admission conjunction is "existing direct-write policy AND effective human-merge admission AND forge permission". Pin-read `packages/core/src/policy/require-human-merge.ts`: `resolveHumanMergePolicy` returns `requireHumanMerge: false, source: "default"` when PROJECT-DEFINITION is absent, when the policy block is absent, and when the flag is unset (documented path 5). It also returns false from `source: "env-bypass"` on `DEFT_ALLOW_BOT_MERGE=1`.

**Failure mode.** An unconfigured consumer satisfies "effective human-merge admission" by having made no decision at all. The remaining two conjuncts are weak: direct-write policy is the thing the Bound already refuses to treat as sufficient alone, and "forge permission" is just a token with push rights — which the automation runner necessarily has. So the strongest limb in the Bound (bot writes directly to the delivery branch, no PR, no review) arms by **default silence**, and the env-bypass variant lets the pushing runner admit itself.

**Why #3791 does not cover this.** The finalize-class carve-out tolerates `requireHumanMerge` effective-false because it is fail-closed scoped to a head class — `isDurableFinalizeHeadRef` on `swarm/finalize/*`, with a PR and a CI lane still in the path. A direct push to the delivery branch has no head class to scope and no PR to observe. `FINALIZE_CLASS_HUMAN_MERGE_ASSUMPTION` is explicit that branch prefix alone never bypasses requireHumanMerge; borrowing its default-false tolerance into a path with no prefix and no PR inverts it.

**Disposition consequence.** Direct-land admission must require a **positively typed** opt-in. `requireHumanMerge` resolving false from `source: "default"`, and `source: "env-bypass"` set on the runner performing the push, MUST NOT count as admission. This is the same shape as the Bound's existing Reject of `allowDirectCommitsToMaster`-alone — that Reject closed one side of the conjunction and left the other open.

### P2 — the pre-land write-guard limb is green by construction in two cases

`blocking` · harvest-changed

The limb (F2, accepted) now reads "Direct-land MUST evaluate completed-write-guard (or equivalent) against the staged commit and refuse push on non-green before history advances". Pin-read says it is **buildable** — `evaluateCompletedWriteGuard(projectRoot, { baseRef })` nets the worktree against the base via `discoverNameStatusRecords` ("Net worktree against the merge base", gluing `base...HEAD` to `git diff HEAD`), so a committed-but-unpushed direct land is evaluable with no new mechanism. Credit where due. Two holes remain.

1. **Vacuous green after push.** With `baseRef` empty or `HEAD`, `resolveDefaultBaseRef` picks `origin/master|main`. On the delivery branch that *is* the push target. Evaluate after the push and the record set is empty, so `code: 0`, green, nothing audited. The limb says "before history advances" but names no base; an implementer who runs the guard in the post-push verification step satisfies the sentence and audits nothing.

2. **Adds-only coverage.** The guard's own header: new `completed/` adds are hard, and "Restamp/mod revalidation of delivery provenance stays #4906 residual — first-ship #5602 closes new adds only", with "Historical corpus at the merge base is not re-audited (doctor advisory)". A direct land that **modifies** an existing `completed/` artifact — the restamp path — passes the guard *by design*, not by luck.

**Disposition consequence.** Two pins, one clause: base is the pre-push remote tip the non-forced push already expects (composes with the Bound's "expected base" limb for free), and direct-land is scoped to **new `completed/` adds only**, failing closed on mod/restamp paths until #4906 residual closes. Without both, the limb's fail-closed property is nominal — it reads as a control and behaves as a formality.

### P3 — the finalize claim cannot serialize the window it is asked to serialize

`blocking` · harvest-changed

The coalesce limb (F3, accepted) now reads "Trigger acquires finalize claim and coalesces merges inside a short window into one cohort". Pin-read: `finalizeClaimRef(label, prNumbers, storyTokens)` returns `swarm/finalize/${deriveFinalizeBranchLabel(...)}`, and `deriveFinalizeBranchLabel` falls through to `safeSegment("pr-" + prNumbers.join("-"))` when no explicit label is passed.

**Failure mode.** Two product PRs merge inside the window. Each triggered run composes a different `prNumbers` set, derives a *different* label, and therefore takes a *different* claim ref. Neither blocks the other. The claim is content-derived, so it cannot serialize a window whose content is exactly what varies. Result: two concurrent finalize heads, overlapping `active/` sweeps, one run's stamp lost to the other's base. The limb is written as if acquiring the claim came first; the shipped helper requires knowing the cohort first.

**Prior art makes the fix trivial.** `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-owed.ts` exports `FINALIZE_OWED_LABEL = "finalize-owed"` — a **constant** label, so `swarm/finalize/finalize-owed` is a stable lane ref that genuinely serializes. The post-merge trigger needs the same shape: a fixed lane label passed explicitly, never cohort-derived.

**It also pays for the P3 idempotency limb.** With a constant lane label, "reuse pending finalize batch" is just: the lane ref already exists, so join it. Without one, "reuse the pending batch" has no stable handle to look the batch up by. One clause buys both limbs. And the Bound's "explicit pending on contention" is then correct as written — with `FINALIZE_CLAIM_STALE_MS` at 2h and claim-stale explicitly *not* PR-stale, a held lane must defer to pending, never steal.

### P3 — the discovery half of the trigger already ships, and the Bound does not name it

`sharpening` · harvest-changed

The Bound's file_scope names `finalize-cohort.ts`, `complete-cohort.ts`, `delivery-evidence.ts`, and the two lifecycle surfaces (F5 landed). It does not name `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-owed.ts` or `packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts`.

`swarm:finalize-owed` (#4919) is "discover and finish ownerless Tracking stories", tip-scanned on the `productPullRequest` mark over `TIP_NONTERMINAL + completed`, with twin checks on `pairingKey` / `planIdentity` and claim refs shared with finalize-cohort. That is, almost exactly, "find merged product work whose lifecycle completion is owed" — the discovery half of the post-merge trigger. It is already wired into `session/session-start.ts` and `runtime/src/session-start.ts`, so the trigger-invokes-existing-land pattern has a shipped precedent this Bound is re-deriving.

**Failure mode.** An implementer reading the Bound builds a second owed-work discoverer inside the trigger. That contradicts the Bound's own P3 principle ("reuse writers only; automation is the trigger + publication policy, not a new completion format") at the discovery layer rather than the write layer, and leaves two code paths that can disagree about what is owed.

**Disposition consequence.** Name finalize-owed as the discovery surface and session-start as the invocation precedent in file_scope; state that the post-merge trigger is a second caller of the owed-discovery path, not a new one.

### P4 — the limb is disclosure, not relief, and the evidence needs hygiene

`footnote`

Two small points, both operative.

1. **Naming.** "relieves: P4 — Document measured overhead and the #6203 / batched-activation dependency" documents the overhead; it does not reduce it. Nothing in this Bound moves the P4 number — by the Bound's own P2 honest-limit line, PR+CI count relief waits on #6203. The limb is sound as a *disclosure* obligation and should be labelled one: `discloses: P4`, not `relieves: P4`. Four `relieves:` against four pains reads as full coverage; the real coverage is two relieved in part, one absorbed, one disclosed.

2. **Evidence hygiene on a public artifact.** The P4 measurement rests on one consumer release (0.129.6) plus an internal benchmark. A single release is an observation, not a measurement, and the Bound should not carry it as AC-grade. The documentation this limb commits to lands in public `content` docs / CHANGELOG: the internal benchmark must be attributed as **internal benchmark evidence (private)**, with neither the benchmark nor the internal strategy work named there. As written, "document measured overhead" invites an implementer to copy the issue body's framing verbatim into a public doc.

Yes — after four clauses, none of which re-architects anything. Every fix reuses a helper already in the tree (`FINALIZE_OWED_LABEL`'s constant-label shape, the guard's `baseRef` option, `resolveHumanMergePolicy`'s `source` field, finalize-owed's discovery). The Bound is under the Thin Fail-Closed bar at the limb level; what it is missing is the pin that makes each limb bite against the specific helper it names.

I considered arguing that the direct-land limb should be cut now and the Bound reduced to trigger + batched finalize-cohort + honest P2 limit — strictly thinner, no new write authority, and both P2 blocking findings evaporate. I did not, for the Round-1 reason: at 1:1 activation that leaves P2 with nothing but an honesty statement, and #680 would close having relieved only agent turns. But the finding count is itself evidence — the direct-land limb generates most of the fail-closed surface in this Bound. If #6203 lands first and collapses activation, direct-land stops earning its complexity and should be dropped rather than specified.

## Steelman of the position I am pressing against

Strongest case that the three blocking findings are over-tight: each is something a competent implementer would discover on first contact with the code — the claim ref's signature is right there, the guard's header says adds-only in its own words, and no one wires a bot push to the delivery branch without checking what admitted it. Carrying all three as Bound clauses is belt-and-braces against a reader who was going to read the file anyway. **What would flip me:** evidence that this Bound's consumers read the named files before writing, which would make these review comments rather than contract. I press anyway because the Bound's whole premise is that automation now performs a step a human used to perform — and the human was the thing catching these. Removing the human is exactly when the implicit checks need writing down.

- finalize-cohort.ts maps null label to pr-<numbers>; an explicit fixed label names a different ref.
- session/session-start.ts invokes that same discovery for its owed gate.

Counterexample: trigger T owns swarm/finalize/<fixed> and has a batched finalize PR for story S. An existing finalize-owed caller inventories S, checks swarm/finalize/pr-N, misses T, and can acquire that different ref and start another finalization. The session gate likewise cannot recognize the fixed batch as S's in-flight owner. The fixed lane serializes trigger instances, but not the existing caller against the trigger.

Non-forced publication limits races; this is not a claim of inevitable data loss. It is a duplicate-work/duplicate-PR path against P3 idempotency and the P2 overhead objective.

Required clause: shared discovery and every admitted finalization caller must recognize the same ownership for included stories before writing. Retain/acquire existing per-story claims beneath the fixed coalescing lane, or make the existing path recognize that lane and its membership. ## Problem

In the current vBRIEF/evaluation workflow, completing a phase/scope often requires a separate follow-up PR whose only purpose is lifecycle bookkeeping: moving the vBRIEF from `active/` to `completed/`, flipping status metadata, updating the project registry, and updating the resume queue.

Concrete example:

- Bridge PR #16 merged the actual editor coverage implementation.
- Bridge PR #17 exists only to complete the lifecycle handoff for that already-merged scope: https://github.com/deftai/bridge/pull/17/changes

This feels inefficient in practice, especially for time and token usage. The implementation/review PR is already done, but the workflow requires another branch, PR body, CI/Greptile cycle, review/status checks, and merge just to mark the phase complete.

## Why this matters

The extra lifecycle PR adds overhead without much product/code value:

- more agent turns and token usage
- another CI/review cycle
- more stacked-branch complexity
- more merge/rebase bookkeeping
- more time before the resume queue accurately reflects the next task

The bookkeeping is important, but the current mechanism feels too expensive for routine phase completion.

## Request

Please evaluate whether Directive should provide a lower-overhead way to finalize a phase/scope after the implementation PR merges.

Possible directions:

1. Include lifecycle completion in the implementation PR before merge.
   - Pros: one PR per scope.
   - Cons: merge metadata (`merged_pr`, `merged_commit`) is not known until after merge.

2. Allow a lightweight post-merge direct commit or bot commit for lifecycle metadata.
   - Pros: avoids a full PR/review cycle for mechanical bookkeeping.
   - Cons: may conflict with branch protection or audit expectations.

3. Split known-before-merge and known-after-merge lifecycle fields.
   - Implementation PR can move the vBRIEF to a `ready-to-complete` or `merged-pending-metadata` state.
   - A later automation fills `merged_pr` / `merged_commit`.

4. Add Directive automation for lifecycle completion.
   - Given a merged PR and scope slug, automatically move the vBRIEF, update registry metadata, and update resume docs.
   - Could create a bot PR only when branch protection requires it, or commit directly when allowed.

5. Reconsider whether `merged_pr` / `merged_commit` must live inside repo-tracked vBRIEF metadata at all.
   - If GitHub is the source of truth for merge metadata, maybe the vBRIEF lifecycle can be completed before merge and avoid post-merge mutation.

## Desired outcome

A documented recommended workflow that preserves traceability but avoids requiring a full separate PR for purely mechanical phase completion whenever possible.
